utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning. Would you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Counsel Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Open session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Par:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kesic.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To start with, will you tell the Court your name, and tell us a little about yourself: Where and when you were born, your occupation, your qualifications, where you are employed, that you are a forensic expert, and so on.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: My name is Blaz Kesic. I was born on the 12th of November, 1948, in Vranci, Kresevo municipality. I completed secondary school for surveyors in 1963 to '67 and acquired the title of surveyor. I have been working as a land surveyor since 1967 in Kiseljak municipality -- and until the 1st of December, 1972, actually, when I moved to Vitez municipality -- and I have been working in that municipality since. I am now head of the cadaster service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, since when you have been a forensic expert.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Since I passed the appropriate examination and had three years of service, and practical experience; that is, ever since 1970.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you remind us since when you have been working for the needs of Vitez municipality?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Since the 1st of December, 1972.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us how familiar you are with the terrain in and around the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: The region of Ahmici, Pirici, and other villages is a region very familiar to me because on a number of occasions I would be called to map out plots there and to register the route of roads and water systems that were being built in those areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the request of the Defence of Vlatko Kupreskic, you have provided your expert opinion. Would you please tell us, what was the task assigned to the expert? Could you please perhaps read it out, because it's a brief one.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: "Request of the Defence." I'm going to read that request that I received from the Defence of Vlatko Kupreskic. "For the needs of trial proceedings IT-95-16-T which is being conducted before the International Tribunal in The Hague, please provide an expert opinion regarding the following: Expert witness task 1: It is necessary to establish, based on the aerial map we enclose, Prosecutor's Exhibit Number 101, the exact position on the terrain in Ahmici of point F, which marks the spot where Fata Pezer's body was, according to the testimony of a witness heard. 2: It is necessary to perform the appropriate measurements and prepare maps indicating position F, as well as a topographical map with a cross section of altitudes relative to Vlatko Kupreskic's house. 3: It should be explained in the opinion in what way position F was established, and answer the question whether there is optical visibility between position F and Vlatko Kupreskic's house, and if not, why? Is it due to the condition of the terrain, woods, or man-made objects? Borislav Krajina, attorney at law." (as read)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, in simple terms, we asked you, on the basis of an aerial photograph, to compare a certain point with the position of Vlatko Kupreskic's house on the ground and the relationships between the two points.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Could we place on the ELMO Prosecutor's Exhibit 101? It is an aerial photograph. In the meantime, I should like to say that this aerial photograph was the one on which Witness F marked a point as indicating the position where he found Fata Pezer's house (sic). We call that point that he made with a marker "point F" so that we know which point we are talking about, and we will now able to see that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, I think there's an error in the transcript. In the translation, it says "... position where he found Fata Pezer's house." I think that should read, in English, "Fata Pezer's body."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaxill.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we have Exhibit 101 on the ELMO? Could it be moved to the right a little, please. Further to right. That's fine now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you wait for my question, please. On this map, do we see an indication with a marker with a an -- no, X is in white, but before that, do you see another point marked with a marker?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes, there's a little circle there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the circle that we have called point F, so that we know what we're talking about. So you have before you Prosecutor's Exhibit 101, and this point will be called point F. Mr. Kesic, in accordance with the task assigned to you as an expert, were you able to establish on the ground where this point F is situated?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you briefly explain to us the procedure by which you were able to find this point on the map on the ground?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: I can. On the basis of this aerial photograph, I established the position of point F. Based on the air map, Prosecutor's Exhibit 101, I established in Ahmici point F, using cadaster maps, land registry matches, number 5 of the land registry of the municipality of Ahmici, scale 1 to 2.500, as well as the original photo chart number 20 of the municipality of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's start again; let's make this very clear. You used this aerial photograph and you used your land registry maps, and on that map, on the basis of this aerial photograph, you established the position of point F. Do you have that land registry map, and if so, will you place it on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I should like to provide copies for members of the Trial Chamber, the Prosecution, and my colleagues on the Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the meantime, will you explain to us where on this map is point F, and also will you show us, with the help of the pointer, on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: When on the original plan -- when I compared the original map with exhibit 101 and transpose the position of point F, it is here. Then, in accordance with my assignment, I marked a position in front of Vlatko Kupreskic's house as point F -- V, V. I'm sorry, that's point V.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we know how we indicated those points on the land registry maps. Now, how did you find those points on the ground?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: I took the measurements from the original land registry maps; that is, the distances from the asphalt road leading to the village of Ahmici, or rather the village road, which goes from Upper Ahmici to the cemetery in the north/south direction, and again I measured from that road towards the west, and then I checked the distance from the edge of the private plots of the Pezers on both sides. So I used at least four different measurements to position point F, which I marked with a wooden pole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you used the distances from the land registry maps. Tell us, how accurate are such measurements?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: If I used the scale of 1 to 2.500, it is considered that accuracy is 0.2 millimetres. We know that 0.1 millimetre equals 25 centimetres, so accuracy is plus/minus 25 centimetres. The transposition of those measurements to the ground, in view of the terrain itself, allows an error that is five to six times greater, which means 2 to 2.5 metres. So the accuracy is plus/minus 2 to 2.5 metres, because the terrain is inclined, it is overgrown and wooded; but in very flat terrain, the accuracy is much greater, and maximum error may be half a metre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: The exhibit D47/3. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, what is the difference in altitude between points F and V, in metres, please?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: When I marked point F on the original plan, I read out the elevation point, which is 422,0. This is absolute altitude using state maps. Similarly, point V in front of Vlatko Kupreskic's house is at elevation point 431. So the difference in altitude between these two points is 8,5 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bearing in mind this difference in altitude, did you carry out a longitudinal cross-section of the land?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please look at that longitudinal cross-section? I have copies for Their Honours and the Prosecution. Meanwhile, will you tell us, on the basis of these measures, that is, the difference in altitude and this profile that you drew, you say that there is no visibility between these two points?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D48/3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let us explain this, sir. This cross-section profile, a longitudinal one, we can see Vlatko Kupreskic's house, D, and our point F. Can you tell us, what are these blue lines on this longitudinal cross-section?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Blue lines here in this longitudinal profile indicate the view in front of Vlatko Kupreskic's house in the direction of point F.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these blue lines indicate the possibility of optical visibility if you look in the direction --

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: I drew the blue line from the house from the height of a normal man, so about a metre and a half. So this is 141. Then I drew it from this point, with the reference point being 432,5, and I tried to measure it. But unfortunately there was a hill, there was an elevation in front of me. You can see it, there is this hill, so that I can look over this hill, or not -- that my view is blocked by this hill. That is, my view, as I stand at this upper point at the house to point F, I cannot see because, simply, there is a hill which blocks the view. I even took the top of Vlatko Kupreskic's house, which is at 438,5, and I also tried to see however this imagined line of vision. Again, I cannot reach point F because of this hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe this is quite clear to us. So the blue lines show us the visibility, the red lines show where there isn't, and we realise there is this hill which blocks the line of vision?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: I also tried to measure at the point 142,5 direction from point F, and I realised that this again comes against this hill, both the ground floor and the top of the house. In other words, from point F you cannot see again either the -- there is an no optical visibility between point F and point V, which is the house of Vlatko Kupreskic, again basically because of the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Now, can we again show a videotape of only about two minutes, showing this place on the ground and the manner in which you marked the particular spot? Mr. Usher, will you please take care of this? As this is being prepared, let us go into private session, please, just for a minute or so, because a name of a protected person is mentioned on the tape. So could we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The videotape will be D48/3. (Private session)

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: (Open session)

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: My task, as a land surveyor, was to take the team that was making the recording to the scene, that is, Vlatko Kupreskic's house, to the other house and to the point F, and to show them the direction from point V to point F, and we have already said that there was no optical visibility between them. I did it in my office on the original map. From point F, I drew a line to the north and formally established line between point F. Then I read out the angle from north to the line between V to F and established that it was 40 degrees to the left. Then I went to the spot, stood at point F, then turned my measuring devices northward by 40 degrees. Then I told them, "Well, this is the direction towards Vlatko Kupreskic's house, so you can record it now," and they did record the view. The reason why we did this outside the place from -- we wanted to establish the position of point F, and we had a stake, a pole, of four metres, and we needed such a tall pole because otherwise we wouldn't be able to take our measurements. The size of 50 times 50, that is the plate that was up there, was showing us the difference. It is four metres above the ground, and if you look carefully in the direction of Vlatko Kupreskic's house, which we could not do in this recording, and if need be we can go back to stop and to show it, where it is on the left, and to the right is this plate, so even a layman can see the difference in altitude between the house and point F or, rather, the elevation between the two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do not think that this is really contestable. It is quite obvious that there is no direct visibility. My question was that you participated in this, that you took those measurements, and you said yes, and that this white plate was positioned precisely at the spot which you indicated and in the direction which is not visible from that particular spot, and you told the cameraman and others in which direction to take the recording. Then we realised that it could not be seen, that is, either the house could not be seen from point F, nor from the house one could see point F. Now, let us now look at another tape, which is D45/3, on which our witness Stipan Vidovic is showing that particular spot. I hope we shall have more luck with this recording.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could the court deputy please -- sorry to interrupt you. Could the court deputy please give us the number of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be marked D49A/3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: (Voiceover) I am Stipan Vidovic, and this is Smajo Pezer's house. When I heard there was a corpse in the woods, I crossed this meadow, entered the wood, and saw the corpse. As I went deeper into the woods, I saw the corpse. I came closer to try to see who that was, and I immediately recognised Fata Pezer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Stipan, please, from this place where you found Fata Pezer's body, will you please tell me whether you can see Vlatko Kupreskic's house from this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You cannot see Vlatko's house from here because of this tall hill here, and there's this wood, so you can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: So there is a hill there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there is a hill, there is a stream and the woods. You can't see it at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kesic, can you tell us whether the spot indicated by this witness is identical with or is different from the place we called point F?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: This spot indicated by Stipan Vidovic is different from point F indicated by me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please tell us what is the difference, what is the difference between the place which you marked as point F and the spot indicated by Mr. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: When identifying point F, I covered the ground in great detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, will you please tell us what is the difference?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: The difference between them in a horizontal line is 30 metres, in the east-west direction they are, so that there's about 30 metres difference between them in the east-west direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The point shown by Mr. Vidovic, is it closer by 30 metres to the house or further, to the Pezers' house?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: It is nearer to Pezer's house by 30 metres, but we're not talking about the altitude difference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So point F is farther away from Pezer's house by 30 metres on the same horizontal line. How did you establish that?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Let me repeat once again, I had to take very detailed measurements from the public road, or rather from the village road and the private plot of Sakib Pezer's, from this house, in this direction, so that I covered that ground several times, looking at the photo recordings. You could see trees cut and stumps. This is the private wood of Smajo Pezer -- which was felled either during or after the war, I don't know -- whereas point F is in the public woods, on public land. This is poorer quality, and you do not see that kind of tree stumps; that is, there are no oak tree stumps, and there is only hornbeam and beech. So, as the witness said, about 15 metres from the end of the meadow into the private woods, and then another 15 metres of this private woods, and then begins the publicly owned wood to my point F. The difference between point S, shown by Stipan Vidovic, and point F is 30 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So are you trying to tell us that knowing the land and by seeing this tape, you could establish which was the spot on the ground which was shown by witness Vidovic? Now I will ask you about the third case. You saw the tape on which the witness showed how he was wounded in the neck, how he was wounded, and so on and so forth. I cannot mention his name because he is protected, but you know which tape I am referring to; the Court also knows which tape I am referring to, so as not to show it for the umpteenth time, since we all know what tape we are talking about. I want now to ask you, do you remember the place which was indicated by the witness as a spot where he was wounded and where other people from the group were wounded? Do you remember the place, or do you not?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. I still remember it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you do remember this spot, could you tell us, how far is that spot which that witness showed, how far is it from the spot which you marked as point F?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Let me call that spot indicated by the witness as point X, and it is not on my point F. It is nearer the state road, or rather the village road, some -- not more than 6 metres away from my spot across the Pezer house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, just wait a moment; one thing at a time. Do we -- let us call that witness CF; that is what he is officially called here. So the place shown by Witness CF is about how far from point F?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Five or six metres away from point F, but in relation to point S, that is, relation to the village road from the village of Ahmici towards the highway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you include these points on your map? If you did, will you please put it on the ELMO, and then I will have two or three more questions to ask you. Now, will you please use your marker to draw by point F the place indicated by Stipan Vidovic -- let us put an S to it -- and the place indicated by Witness CF. So these are three points, these three spots indicated.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes. Point CF is very near, because we were using the scale of 2.500, so five to ten metres means one to two millimetres, not more than that, on the map. So within this green circle, where it says "F," the point CF is right within this green circle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So let me ask you, in the end, all these three points are on one and the same horizontal line?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes, all these three are more or less the same altitude above the sea; that is, 422 to 423. Not more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they all on one and the same path?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes. Stipan Vidovic, when he showed this, he walked down the meadow and reached the woods, and they also, when I measured, went from the house, yes, this is a path which goes from the village of Ahmici down there, and we all followed this path.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Can you see Vlatko Kupreskic's house from any of these points?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: No, there is no optical visibility from any of these points. When we draw the longitudinal profile from this point to Vlatko Kupreskic's house, there is no visibility, nor from point S, nor from the CF point. You cannot see Vlatko Kupreskic's house from any of these points.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I do not have any more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I should like to tender into evidence D47, 48, 49/3, and that the finding and the expert opinion also be admitted into evidence. We already submitted the expert opinion. Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No objection; thank you. They are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D50/3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. This, as well, will be admitted into evidence. Mr. Blaxill, Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Blaxill:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kesic, good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sorry, I assumed there was no cross-examination by Defence counsel. I apologise. Counsel Radovic? Cross-examined by Mr. Radovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that you work as a land surveyor in the land registry department in Vitez municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a surveyor, are you also engaged over disputes between private owners over land?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes. The courts in Bosnia-Herzegovina proceed in such a way that the disputing parties first go to the land registry, and then the surveyor, in the presence of both parties, tries to make a deal outside court, so that minor disputes are resolved on the spot, and we have no written records of such negotiations. We feel that the dispute has been settled over the borderline between individual properties, private properties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the basis of the maps, they tried to re-establish boundaries between lands owned by private individuals?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us what the situation is like in the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever also negotiate boundaries in the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes. As in any other village, during spring, farm work, problems would frequently arise. Sometimes they were minor, sometimes more important. In some cases there were court proceedings, but in most cases we tried to achieve a settlement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the name Sakib Ahmic? Not the one living on the road, but the one further away.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes, he's a driver in Impregnacija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever regulate the boundaries of his land?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes, unfortunately, several times in my 20 years of service. Mr. Sakib Ahmic is a very hardworking man; he tills his land, tends his orchards, but he doesn't respect other people's boundaries. Actually, he never built a hard fence around his property, a wire fence, concrete fence, or any other way that means hard fence, or oak poles with wire, or with wooden planks. So his whole property is marked with a live hedge, natural thorn hedges, blackberry thorns and hornbeam hedge, so that he usually cuts those hedges in such a way as to gain up to 30 centimetres of his neighbour's land. That is one thing that he does. Another thing that he does is when he plows his fields, and as his property is on a slope, all those above him suffer. Why? Because he causes land to be eroded. And he had disputes with his neighbours at least four or five times, with Krdzalic Mehmed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is he by ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: A Muslim. Hrustanovic Mehmed, who is also a Muslim; that is to north of his property. To the west of his property is the Kupreskic property, and to the south is again the Kupreskic property, whereas to the east is a public road. So the property department which is in charge of regulating relations between private and state-owned property frequently had to intervene.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as I understand it, he had disputes over land boundaries with all his neighbours, regardless of those neighbours' ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, did you have any disputes or problems with him since these young men have been in prison?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes, about a month ago, Luca Kupreskic came to the office and said, "What am I going to do? Sakib is clearing away the land. He wants to rebuild his house. He's cutting the fruit and planting, but as usual, he's clearing his hedges so that next to Zoran's house, he has dug in a pole right inside his property." So if the hedge is 50 or 60 metres wide, instead of putting the pole in the middle of that hedge, he digs it in to the left side of the hedge, which means closer to his neighbour. Mrs. Luca noticed this and said, "The children are away; I don't want to intervene; let it stand. But when the time comes, we will start some kind of court proceedings and regulate our boundaries for good." So in spite of all that has happened, the disputes continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now tell us, who is Luca?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Luca Kupreskic is Zoran's mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, will you please get up and look at this aerial photograph? You have to use the other headphones. Look at the photograph first; I don't think you've seen it before. Show the Vitez/Busovaca road, please.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: (Indicating)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now show us the road that branches off towards Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: This is the asphalt road, the old school (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And going along that road from the main road towards Ahmici, to your right in that same direction -- listen to my question, please. Moving along that road, from the intersection upwards, to the right of that road, whose houses are there?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: These are all Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, to the right of that road are exclusively Muslim houses?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes, and a few on the left-hand side. A maximum of five houses. This is the Vidovic property, the Kupreskic property.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the left-hand side; I'm talking about the right-hand side of the road.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: To the right of the road, this entire settlement consists of Muslim households.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. I have noticed that there was some confusion over land registry books, because we are obviously in a different legal systems, the Prosecution and us, so perhaps I could ask you a few questions about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit P358, I think. Copy of the certificate of possession.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please explain to the Court how these things are regulated in Vitez municipality, when it says "Cadastral District, Travnik"?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: The cadaster district is a broader area which encompasses several municipalities. This district is formed on the basis of the geography of the terrain, which means that people living in a certain geographic area have their meadows and fields plotted out in the same way. So the cadaster districts are determined by geographic and political considerations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But how did Vitez come under Travnik? When was that cadaster district formed, the cadaster district?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Ever since the establishment of districts, in the socialist system, there was the Travnik, Bugojno, and Zenica districts and the municipalities that came under them, under the district court of Travnik, which had the land registry books for Travnik, Novi Travnik, Vitez. So we were part of that district.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us the purpose of the cadaster, and what does it show?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: The purpose is to keep records of areas, crops, quality of land, and the owners of property, so as to able to collect taxes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the priority role is to have a record of taxpayers who own a mobile property?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So tell us the difference between the cadaster and the land registry books.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: The difference is that the land registry books keep records of the owners, which was identical to those who were in possession. But when Austro-Hungary formed the cadaster in Bosnia-Herzegovina, life changes, inheritance, sales, resulted in changes, so that the buyers and sellers did not register in the land books all these transactions, mainly to avoid paying taxes, because a third of the value had to be paid as taxes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, these cadaster numbers of plots, in Vitez, do they coincide, the numbers in the cadaster and the numbers in court?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Vitez, like all Bosnian cadasters, have been subjected to changes of numbering twice. The reason was that the Austro-Hungarian land books were formed in 1888, and the land registry and the cadaster, the numbers in those two documents were identical. This continued until 1945, and then during the Second World War, many cadaster plans were burnt, and destroyed in some cases; also the land registry books. Sometimes the whole book, sometimes only certain segments. With time, it was necessary to have a record of the possession, so a list was made simply of the owners of various plots. This kind of register is called the cadaster of possession. This was in force until the '70s, when large-scale construction of roads, factories, et cetera, led to a situation when a new registration could be made, new aerial photographs were taken, and this is a copy. That is when the maps were made in the scale 1 to 2.500, so we had complete plans on the basis of which we could continue with construction and have a proper record of land ownership. So the same plot would acquire a third number for Ahmici municipality. According to the municipal cadaster, it was 5/56, forest, stream; according to the Austro-Hungarian books, it was 132/1. So the numbers changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you well -- let us not go into the details. I just wanted to make it clear to the Court and the Prosecutor how these records were kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do not have any questions. I had just intended to announce my learned friend, Mr. Ranko Radovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Blaxill?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Blaxill:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kesic, good morning to you, sir. My name is Michael Blaxill. I'm one of the prosecuting counsel assigned to this case. May I ask you, you clearly have some experience in dealing with court cases involving land disputes. Have you been called upon to testify in criminal proceedings on many occasions before?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me how many?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: At the Travnik court, maybe 10 to 15 times, and it had to do with felling of woods, to prove whether a tree in private ownership had been felled or in social ownership, that kind of case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Thank you very much. Sir, when you first addressed the issue of finding the point marked "F" on the ground, I believe it was the aerial photograph that you were supplied; is that correct? We've seen it this morning. Is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that on there, the civilian witness in question has drawn a fairly large circle, I think a smallish cross somewhere in that circle, and written the words "Dead body" in English? Does that appear on there? Well, I should correct that question slightly. That annotation of the words has actually been added as an identifying feature later, but would the original photograph that you received, sir, have that circle on it?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you say that on the ground, that would represent a fair area of territory, a few metres, would it not, within that circle?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: This circle that I was given, its radius is about five metres. Transposed to the ground, it would be about four to five metres across.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And at that time, you were not made aware of the other points that we've seen revealed through other witnesses in the videotapes today? You did not know that when you commenced your work?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: No. My first task was based on Prosecutor's Exhibit 101. Then I went on the ground, and then the camera came to film it. Later on, I was shown S and X, the two witnesses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in point of fact, sir, do you recall also what scale the photograph was which you then compared with the land registry map?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: The photograph was 1 to 2.500, roughly, and I can prove that by comparing the original map with -- and covering it with the transparency, and comparing it with 101, and using my own original photo sketch during an aerial photography in 1970, which is again the scale of 1 to 2.500.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course, therefore, the terrain and the contours that you're working to date back to 1970 information; that is correct? I've heard you correctly?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: No -- yes, partly. But also I personally went there. There was no asphalt road in 1970; now there is. There were no fences; now we have them. Vlatko's house was not there; now we have it. These are the buildings that were built subsequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And turning, if I may, now, sir, to your cross-sectional diagram that takes us from point F to the house of Vlatko Kupreskic, would I be correct in assuming that you have taken different points from the contours of the map, and they have been joined, effectively, with straight lines to create the diagram? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Working across the cross-section diagram you have prepared, would it be true to say that you have taken particular points of height reference from the map, and they have been joined by you with, effectively, straight lines on this diagram? Is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So indeed, the actual terrain, as we've seen from the videos, would look somewhat different, with other little dips and bumps between the high points; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes. My cross-sectional profile was done in the scale -- M equals 1 to 100 to 200, which means the altitude was in scale 1 and the length, 200, for better visibility. Each point on the longitudinal profile, zero at Vlatko's house, then 6 metres, then 12 metres, then the elevation of the ground. Then point V, and then, in the lowest level, we have the land contour, and it says from O to 12 metres is the yard. From 12 to 18 is the asphalt road, as can be seen on the profile. Then there is pastures, which has a mild dip. Then it climbs mildly at the 28th metre. Then there's a meadow that goes up to 45 metres in height, then again a mildly upward-sloping meadow, then pastureland that covers a hill. Then we go to point 84, with a low-growing trees. Then it goes downhill, and at a level of 14 metres, there is elevation point 430. Then we have elevation point 427,5; then a mild slope, going towards point F, at a length of 120 metres. So this is the terrain as if it were cut across and we would see it from the side. A cross-section, in other words.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now taking that view, you have point V. Where, physically, did you take that point on the house of Vlatko Kupreskic, because it appears to be a spot to one side of the property on the cross-section. Could you indicate where, on the house, you took that measurement from?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: We have to go back to the other map, to place it on the ELMO, indicating points F, S and X. This is the old house of Vlatko Kupreskic, his father's, and this is the newly-built house. Point V is between the old and new house of Vlatko Kupreskic in the yard where there is a table and chairs, so it is between these two houses, where I was taken by the Prosecutor (sic), to show the angle from which the film was taken -- I'm sorry, not the Prosecutors, the Defence counsel, I'm sorry -- to show me the angle for filming this point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you indicate or do you recall, sir, the difference between -- the distance, I'm sorry, between those two houses?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: The distance between the two houses is roughly 15 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say the point you picked was probably therefore seven and a half metres to one side, if you were halfway between the two?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: It was about five metres from the new house, because there's a plateau there, it is flat, there's a table and chairs, there's a water tap, and then there's a mild slope going downwards, downhill towards the old house. So this is the most dominant position between the old and new house, the yard of Vlatko Kupreskic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree, sir, looking at your diagram, the house has something like a ten-metre width? According to this plan, would that be about right, sir?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct that it is probably another eight metres from the wall of the house to the far side of the asphalt road beside the house? Would that be correct from your diagram? I think it takes us up to about an 18-metre point there, doesn't it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes, but this diagram shows the direction between point V and point F. If we go back to the map, let me show it to you, you will see the old house and the new house and the direction, and we will see the road going on. So from the cross-section, the house is moved away upwards, and our vision is going downwards. But for practical reasons, I had to draw the house as if it was actually in the line of vision. But actually the house is left to the side. We are looking in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would that place the house a little more towards the hill that we see over on the right side of your diagram? Would that, in reality, make the house a little nearer there?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: No. The relationship between point V and F and the position of the house, according to this line, fully shows point V, the house, and point F. The only reason, and I'm going back to the map again to show it to you, the house is mildly turned 15 degrees away from the line, it is at an angle of 15 degrees, I have to show it in this way in the cross-section. But this map shows the actual position of the buildings and the line linking point F and point V.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I can recap, sir, basically speaking, what we have here is point F, that is based on the marking of a photograph by one witness to have appeared in this Tribunal, I believe that is so, and a cross-section that in fact forces you, by its nature, if you like, to distort the reality of the layout. You have to do that in order to perform this function; is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: No, I did not distort anything. What I did was draw in the house. I brought it closer to the line in order to show the altitudes. The most important thing here is altitudes and the ratios of distances between individual points, so that I come back to this -- we had to come back to this map to look at the directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I wasn't suggesting that you would wilfully distort the reality. What I'm saying is with the limitations placed upon you, you had to make the house at a different angle from its real position. But I appreciate and understand what you mean, sir. Now, from this --

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If one were to say there were people standing on that asphalt road adjacent to the Kupreskic house, and if we had some people on the slope facing that house, the obvious thing would appear that there is a clear line of sight between such groups of people. Would you agree with me, sir?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes, up to the top of the hill, in front of Vlatko Kupreskic's house, all that is in front of Vlatko Kupreskic's house, both from the ground floor and the top of the house, but as of point V. When you go to the horizon when you reach point V, then you can't see it. But down to 84, which you see on the longitudinal profile, and 432 height reference, you can see Vlatko Kupreskic's house and the road in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, I'm just going to put to you a brief theory. I suggest, sir, if we have heard evidence perhaps in this courtroom that people were moving along the lower part of the slope facing Vlatko Kupreskic's house, and if those people say they saw soldiers in front of the house, i.e., on their side, between them and Kupreskic's house, a line of sight would be clear between the group of soldiers by the house and the people at the foot of the slope. We're quite clear on that, aren't we, sir, if that's the case?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: If they were moving in the direction from Vlatko Kupreskic's house towards point F through the meadow, and I'm coming back to the situation on the ground, 442,5 is here. If they crossed the asphalt road, then this meadow, they are within the field of vision. But as soon as they've crossed 432,5 point and start downhill, then they are outside the field of vision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, they would be in vision as well if they were walking horizontally along. As if we were walking into the diagram, that way, they would still be visible at the bottom of this ridge, would that be correct, heading that way or this way?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: The borderline, the horizon, goes -- follows the contours of the hill. If this storage or, rather, Vlatko Kupreskic's house, old or new -- this is point F. This is the old and the new house of Vlatko Kupreskic. This here is point F, and as a land surveyor who has been reading these aerial photographs all the time, I think I can read this map even without the tridimensional goggles, and I can see that this is the hill. So this is the slope and the meadow, and point F is here. That is on this side of the field of vision from Vlatko Kupreskic's house, and I walked from here to the meadow, to the pasture land, to the woods, down to the field of vision and to the foot of the hill. All that is on this side is visible, and below that you cannot see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honours, I'm mindful of the time. Did you want to take a break at this juncture or did you want to run until 10.45?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Let's take a break at quarter to 11.00, because we will have to stop at 1.00, to my regret. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, thank you for establishing that, sir. Has anybody suggested to you previously that that might be a version of events relating to the persons whose names I won't mention but the ladies who got injured and killed? Has that version of events ever been told to you before as a theory?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you then indicate, sir, just confirm, that if we're looking at the side of the asphalt road facing the slope in the direction of point F, to the base of that slope we have something in the region of 40 or so metres, is that about right, from the edge of the road across to the bottom of the slope?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: Yes, because the reference point is 18 -- yes, there would be 40 metres, the whole of 40 metres of meadow, grazing land and meadow, from the foot of the hill to up the slope where pasture land begins. That is about 40 metres, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a couple of very brief further matters, sir. On the sound track of the videotape we saw today, the one which shows your marker post and the reference points on it, you refer to a certain person being wounded and a body being found at that given spot. Would you agree, sir, that that is clearly only on one piece of information that you had at the outset in your brief?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ KESIC
utterances.text: As I watched the tape, I learned the same thing as you can hear on the tape. That is, that it is the point F that we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I'm obliged to you for answering my questions, sir. Thank you. Mr. President, Your Honours, I conclude.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I have no more questions. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So therefore we have no questions. Mr. Kesic, thank you for coming to The Hague to give evidence in court. You may now be released. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We will now take a break, and when we resume in 30 minutes, we will have, I hope, the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, the next witness is Mr. Catipovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Mr. Skavic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning. Will you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: You may be seated. Counsel Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Par:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Skavic.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please give us first your name, your date and place of birth, the education that you had, your occupation, the jobs you were employed in formerly, where do you work now, and for how long have you been a forensic expert witness?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: My name is Josip Skavic. I was born in 1943 in Pakrac, the Republic of Croatia. After the secondary school, I enrolled in the Faculty of Medicine. I graduated from it in 1967, and sometime in 1970 I began to work at the Forensic Medicine Institute at the Faculty of Medicine. I completed my specialisation in forensic medicine, and then I continued a specialisation in pathology. And after the completion of that specialisation course, I continued to work at the Forensic Medicine Institute, and that is where I am to this day. At present, I am associate professor at the Faculty of Medicine in Zagreb, and I have been a forensic expert witness for the past 20 years or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The Defence counsel of Vlatko Kupreskic has asked you for your expert opinion. Will you please tell us, what was it that you were asked to do?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: The subject of my expert analysis were the injuries of two persons, that is, (redacted) and (redacted). We were asked about the injuries they sustained, to do a joint expert analysis with a ballistic expert, that is, a so-called interdisciplinary expert analysis, and this was done with Damir Catipovic, an engineer. Another task was to establish the mechanism, that is, the means with which the wounds were inflicted, and if the injuries were due to firearms. Then we also had to establish what kind of weapon was responsible for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you please now tell us, what documents did you have at your disposal? I will give them to you one by one, and I shall ask you to comment on them or, rather, explain what each of these documents represents. Before that, will you please tell us if you personally examined any of the two injured persons?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: Two days ago, I examined (redacted), one of the injured persons, or rather I examined the scars which are still visible after the wounds were healed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, will you please show this document to Professor Skavic?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is D51/3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Mr. Skavic, will you please tell us, what kind of document is this?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: What you have here is the discharge list of the medical centre in Travnik where (redacted), the injured person, was at the traumatology and surgical ward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, when was that?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: She was admitted to hospital on the 16th of March, '93, to the 15th of -- to the 3rd of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Could we have the second document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document D52/3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Professor, this is a discharge list of the 17th Mountain Brigade army of Bosnia-Herzegovina which shows that patient (redacted) was treated in the hospital between the 16th of March, 1993, until the 10th of May, 1993. Thank you. We have another list.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit D53/3.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: This is a finding of a specialist relative to the examination of (redacted) on the 18th of March, 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let us talk about the injury sustained by this person. What was the degree of injuries and the type of injuries that you found in (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: After examining in view of the treatment of patient (redacted), we found the injuries as those made by firearms in the upper leg and lower leg right, an open fracture of the right scapula, and there were alien metal bodies found. So this was evidently an open complicated fracture of the right lower leg. We normally call it a severe injury. In the upper leg, the injury was not described. We do not have the findings on the injuries to the tissues or to the muscles or to the bone. We conclude that this was a light bodily injury.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And about (redacted), what kind of injuries did you find there?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: After examining the injured person, (redacted) (redacted), the injury was described as that of the right side of the neck and the right side of the back. The neck injury looks like a groove; that is, the injury to soft tissues, 16 times 2 centimetres. To the right, in the shoulder blade -- that is, the scapula -- it was a wound 5 times 3 centimetres large. I would like to relate it to the examination that I mentioned a while ago. On the basis of this medical documentation, on the basis of which I examined him and then wrote my opinion, I expressed a suspicion that these could have been two projectiles; that is, two wounds independent one of another. This derives from the topographical relationship of the two wounds. If we look at the neck injury and the scapular injury, it would seem that the latter projectile should have caused major injury. I thought this these were two independent ones, but when I examined it, we see that in the medical documentation, the injury on the right side of the back was wrongly localised. It was described as the one in the region of the scapula, but it is above the shoulder blade, rather. Since the wound was inflicted there, we concluded that it was one single injury; that is, an injury which began at the right side of the neck as a tangential scratch, and after that the projectile entered the soft tissues of the right shoulder and then ended in an exit wound described as the size 5 times 3 centimetres above the right shoulder blade. If we look at this injury, it seems that this direction, if we look at the body in the upright position, then the bullet passed from above, then to the back and down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us, what means could have caused that injury?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of features of this injury and the still-visible scars, it is not impossible to forensically establish the means whereby this wound was inflicted. It could be due either to small firearms or the shrapnel fragment of some fragmentation bullet, or something like that. I still cannot establish with certainty what kind of means was used, but that groove which was caused in the injury would seem to indicate a wound caused rather by a shrapnel than by a projectile from a firearm, because in the latter case, the groove would have been much narrower. I'm referring to the tangential injury, which would then correspond to the calibre of the particular weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were trying to come to some conclusions as to the weapons, did you consult a ballistics expert?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: I must point out that what I have just said was based only on the examination of the injuries; that is, I base my opinion, my finding, on the description of the injury.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you now tell us, in your expert opinion, from what direction could the injury have been inflicted?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: I can refer only to the relationship between the source of the shrapnel, of the fragment, and the injury already said that the direction, the direction -- if we see the body of the injured person upright, then it came from upward, then went backward and downward. So whether he was standing, sitting, lying down, turned to the left or to the right, these ratios have to be identical. So once again I can say, if it was firearms that were used, then we're taking the barrel. If it was a fragment, then it came from in front of him downward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you exclude the possibility that these injuries could have been due from a shot fired from the back and to the left?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: If I look at these relationships, the only possibility, if it was a firearm, that the barrel was in front and upward. No other relationship could have resulted in such an injury.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think it is possible that such an injury was due to a fragment of a fragmentation bullet which hit, for instance, the trunk of a tree above the injured and in front of him?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that there is such a possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the case of (redacted), what is the situation as regards the direction from which the injury was inflicted?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: The injured (redacted) sustained injuries in her right leg; that is, both the upper and lower leg. The medical documentation does not give us any detailed description of the injury, so that we cannot say where was the entry wound or as to the channel, and possibly the exit wound, if it was a bullet which went through. Now, this localisation of two injuries of a rather small part of the body -- that is, the right leg -- seems to suggest that the injury was due, if it was a small firearm, so either a bullet or the shrapnel, it should mean that the epicentre of the explosion was on the right-hand side, and I cannot say whether it was strictly right laterally, right front, right anterior, or right posterior. I can only say that it came from the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can announce that the expert witness will be examined by Mrs. Jadranka Slokovic-Glumac and by Mr. Ranko Radovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Ms. Slokovic-Glumac:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, professor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I should like the usher to show the witness Prosecution Exhibit P84 through to P96.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Professor, these are photographs taken in a certain area in a house, and I should like to ask you to look at those photographs and to tell us whether you see on these photographs the bodily remains of human victims.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Can we put them on the ELMO, please, at least one of the photographs?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: I should like to select some of these photographs, this one as the first one, because I think it is important to see that this was a burning in a dwelling, and obviously the floor -- the ceiling caved in. Then I can assert with certainty, and I think this is obvious even to a layman, that we see a part of a human skeleton or the remains of a dead body. There are several photographs showing rather masses of parts which could be a dead human body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we say with certainty that each of those black masses shown on these photographs represent a human body?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: No. That is why I said that such a picture can be seen in the case of the burning of biological material. It can be any biological material, which means a human body, but it can also be an animal. So I have to stress that in such situations, these are highly-delicate issues to provide an expert opinion on. We have to establish whether it is human tissue, which is then further examined by pathologists. In addition to this obvious human skeleton that I have just drawn attention to and which is shown on several of these photographs, for example, here and then the same thing here on this photograph, it can be said with certainty that these are human remains, and on the basis of this, that is all that I could say. I couldn't say anything more than that, underlining the delicacy of the problem and which it is difficult to provide an expert opinion on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But by examining these photographs, could you say how many persons may have been involved?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: Underlining what I have already said, how difficult it is to provide an expert opinion, I think that no expert could, on the basis of these photographs and the first impression one has seeing them, could go that far. I think that it is very difficult to take samples because of the caving in of the ceiling, and only after lengthy studies, which would include anthropological and forensic and other studies, could any conclusions be made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But in view of the fact that you are a highly-experienced forensic expert, the fact if you had been on the spot at the time the photographs were taken, could you have been able to say with certainty at the time, by visual examination, what it was?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: No, I would never be so bold as to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So regardless of your experience, even then it would be guesswork, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the only way to establish the number of victims involved would be a proper forensic study, combined with anthropological and other studies? I don't know what else you would need.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: Certainly we would require teamwork, which would certainly include an anthropologist, a forensic expert, a laboratory to determine the [indiscernible] necessary and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Professor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I have only one question for you. Cross-examined by Mr. Radovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us who has the right to interpret medical documentation?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: Only a doctor, or if it is a kind of a trial involved, then a forensic medical expert, a doctor who establishes a diagnosis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can medical documentation and the condition of a patient at any point in time be interpreted by a person who is not a doctor?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: I can only speak about the customary interpretations that we have in the Republic of Croatia. It is excluded for any other kind of expert to interpret medical documentation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can a social worker interpret medical documentation?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Radovic. Counsel Blaxill.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Blaxill:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Professor, good morning to you, sir. My name is Michael Blaxill. I'm one of the prosecuting counsel assigned in this case. I just have a couple of questions, sir, and partly to clear up something that I think I may have misunderstood from you. The gentleman referred to, Mr. (redacted), he suffered the neck and shoulder injury. I'm not quite certain if your eventual conclusion was that this was caused by one projectile or was two separate wounds. Could you just clarify that for me, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: Underlining the examination I carried out two days ago, I said that the conclusion that can be inferred from the written opinion and documentation, in view of the exit wound on the right-hand side of the back, has to be changed, in the sense that they were not two separate wounds but only one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So therefore I think I understand correctly. He was hit by one projectile, with an entry wound and an exit wound, and that's what you saw?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: From the beginning, I pointed out that on the basis of the characteristics of the wound, I cannot say whether it was a small-arms bullet or a fragment, and I say that both is possible. In view of the channel formed by the projectile, I consider it more likely to be a fragment or a shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, I believe you agree, sir, that the wounds are at least consistent with the possibility that this was a bullet from a hand-held firearm of some description. That is one potential option?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: As one of the two possibilities, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As well, Professor, regarding the lady's leg injuries, again would you say they are also consistent with injuries that may have been caused by a projectile from a hand-held firearm or firearms?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: It could have been, among others, caused by the projectile of a hand-held firearm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, Professor, you have not had the opportunity to examine the lady. You're going purely by the documentation that we have seen here today; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP SKAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, only on the basis of medical documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I thank you for that, Professor. Much obliged to you. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaxill. Counsel Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I have no additional questions, but I would like to tender into evidence D51/3, 52/3 and 53/3 at Defence exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. They are admitted into evidence. The Court has no questions for the witness. Professor Skavic, thank you so much for coming here to give evidence in court. You may now be released.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Par, do you know whether there's any other expert witness available?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Catipovic is waiting outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Your Honours, in connection with this particular witness, a report has been submitted already, giving an expert commentary on the performance of a certain firearm, namely an MGV-176 machine gun. That report has been accepted in its entirety by the Prosecution. So if that assists the Court and saves time, I would just remind everybody that we've accepted that particular report in its entire contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaxill. I'm sure that Counsel Par will take this into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Mr. Blaxill mentioned an expert opinion which comes under Mr. Radovic's defence, so our expert witness is testifying to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: [Inaudible] the same expert, but that report was indeed arranged by Mr. Radovic. My apologies, Your Honour. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Catipovic. Would you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Counsel Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Par:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Catipovic. Are we ready to start? Can you hear me well?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR CATIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, everything is fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please tell the Court your name, a few words about yourself, your professional career, where you were born, your education, where you're working, what your present job is, and what experience you have in ballistic expert opinions, and how long you have been an expert in the field?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR CATIPOVIC
utterances.text: I was born in 1945 in Sinj, in the Republic of Croatia. Since 1954, I have been living in Zagreb, where I completed my education, starting from elementary school, on to grammar school, and the Department of Chemistry. I'm a graduate chemical engineer. Since 1973, I have been working in the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia as a ballistic expert and for mechanical trajectories, where I'm still employed, and I'm head of the department for such expert opinions. I have been working for 26 years in the same field, out of which I have been a forensic expert for some 20 years. And in view of my age, obviously I have some experience.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. When I asked you about your experience in the ballistic area, I was thinking of the war in Croatia and whether you had any experience from that war.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR CATIPOVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, as compared to many experts world-wide, you know what happened in our part of the world, this may be a good thing for our profession, so that from the beginning of the events that started in 1990 until 1995, I covered a great deal of ground and saw many instances and many cases in the course of my regular duties in the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The Defence of Vlatko Kupreskic has submitted to you a certain number of documents, maps, videotapes, and asked you to provide your expert opinion. Could you tell this Court what your assignment was as ballistic expert?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR CATIPOVIC
utterances.text: It is true that I was provided documents on the basis of which Dr. Skavic, who has testified just before me, and I were asked to provide combined medical and ballistic expert opinion, and virtually the same questions were addressed to the medical expert and myself, as a ballistic expert. I can repeat them now. Those questions were -- I don't know whether Dr. Skavic repeated them here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me help you so that we shouldn't repeat them or read them here. So I will help you. Your assignment was to jointly provide expert opinions and to analyse the injuries and the causes of those injuries?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR CATIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you establish the mechanism and the means by which the injured were injured?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR CATIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion, can you tell us how those injuries occurred?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR CATIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of documents available to me, there is no doubt that the injuries were caused by a bullet or fragments of a bullet fired from a firearm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion, what was the means used to provoke the injury?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR CATIPOVIC
utterances.text: The means used is a question that it is difficult to answer without material traces, because our opinions are based exclusively on the testimony of witnesses and the effect on the surrounding objects, in this case on the branches of trees and the wounds on the bodies of the injured. On that basis, it is my opinion that it was a firearm of a stronger calibre with fragmentation bullets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say a heavier firearm, what calibre are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR CATIPOVIC
utterances.text: The most frequent infantry weapon is the automatic/semi-automatic rifle or light machine gun. 7,32 -- 7,62 to 39 millimetres are excluded. Everything else could be possible, depending on the distance, including the M-84 machine gun which one of the witnesses refers to. But I am of the opinion that it was something even stronger than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let us clear up this point. Calibres corresponding to a normal rifle, an automatic rifle, are excluded? You feel that they were --

utterances.speaker: DAMIR CATIPOVIC
utterances.text: It was a weapon from an M-84 machine gun, this would be the lowest limit, anything from that and including that upwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Allow me to ask you a few questions that will help us to understand how you reached that conclusion. Let me show you the documents that we supplied you with, and will you please confirm whether you took those documents into consideration and what you concluded from each of them? We gave you the expert opinion of the land surveyor expert. What were you able to see from his finding, and why was it useful to you?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR CATIPOVIC
utterances.text: From the expert opinion of the surveyor, where he gave a cross-section of the area on the basis of an aerial photograph, that is, Prosecutor Exhibit 101, he identified position F, that is, the position where the body was found. Also on the basis of that aerial photograph, he was able to identify the location of Vlatko Kupreskic's house in relation to point F. On the basis of points established in this way, he made a longitudinal cross-section with the configuration and the distances between V and F, and his final conclusion is, when we look at that diagram, that there is no optical vision between point V and point F.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the conclusion that there is no optical vision, does that mean for you, as a ballistic expert, that using an ordinary infantry weapon, it is impossible to hit anyone?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR CATIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is quite certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
